Cillian’s Midnight Dip, X:2

This setting of the tune comes from the “Open The Door For Three” album. On their sleeve notes they call it McDermott’s and say that they got it from CRE4. I couldn’t find the tune in there.

Re: Cillian’s Midnight Dip

This tune is indeed from Breathnach CR4 but it is named “The Pomeroy Fiddler” in my ABC book. The original book was Gan Ainm but the notes attribute it to Michael “the master” McDrrmott so the name McDermott’s seems to be the most common. McDermott was from Pomeroy and Carrigmore.

Curious. Jwiseman above has found this tune in Breandan Breathnach’s CRE Vol. 4. I found it as # 193, “Gan Ainm”, and as JW says, the source is listed as “Master” McDermott who was a fiddle player from Co. Tyrone. Therefore not composed by Cillian Vallely.
Is “Cillian’s Midnight Dip” maybe a collective title for the set ?
Guessing here as I don’t have the “Lunasa” sleeve notes.

Re: Cillian’s Midnight Dip

On Lunasa’s album Redwood, the set is called “Spoil the Dance” consisting of Cillian’s Midnight Dip/Tuttles Reel/Spoil The Dance - all given as traditional.

The notes of CRE4 say, “Another example of his own compositions from the fiddler Michael ‘The Master’ McDermott, Pomeroy and Carrigmore, County Tyrone.”

Opinionated Couch: CRE refers to a five-volume tunebook called “Ceol Rince na h’Eireann, compiled from the collecting of Breandán Breathnach (1912-1985). It is one of the most important collections of traditional Irish dance music, and it’s mentioned a lot on this site, usually by ”CRE".

↳ Posted by Nigel Gatherer on May 31st, 2023.
